editorial:
You get a fresh animated trip into Middle-earth that focuses on Rohan’s fierce history, with Helm Hammerhand facing a deadly revenge plot from Wulf. The story feels like a war tale mixed with family drama, and the hand-drawn style gives it a bold, old-school fantasy look. You follow Helm, his family, and the people of Rohan as they try to survive a siege, so the stakes feel personal and urgent. It is not a quiet fantasy; it is loud, proud, and built around loyalty, anger, and survival.

The action scenes are the biggest draw, especially the battles around the Hornburg, and the voice work gives Helm a strong, stubborn presence. The pacing moves quickly, though some side characters do not get enough time to shine. If you want deep character study, you may feel shortchanged, but if you want swords, speeches, and siege tension, you will have a good time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Helm and his people make their last stand at the Hornburg while Wulf pushes his attack. Helm dies fighting, but his sacrifice helps Rohan hold on long enough for help to matter. The twist is that Wulf’s victory is hollow because his obsession costs him everything, while Helm’s legacy lives on through his family and the fortress that later becomes Helm’s Deep. You see that revenge destroys the attacker, while courage protects the future.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated fantasy battles and Lord of the Rings lore.
